Essential Apps for UK Motorcycle Touring

Your smartphone is the most versatile touring tool you own. With the right apps installed, it handles navigation, weather forecasting, fuel finding, accommodation booking, and route planning. Here are the must-have apps for touring Britain by motorcycle in 2026.

Navigation Apps

  • OS Maps (£24/year): The definitive UK mapping app. Ordnance Survey's 1:25000 maps show every track, path, building, and contour line. Offline downloads are excellent. Essential for rural touring where Google Maps lacks detail.
  • Kurviger (Free / Premium £20/year): Motorcycle-specific routing that actively seeks out curvy, enjoyable roads. Avoids motorways by default. GPX import/export. The premium version adds offline routing and advanced options.
  • Calimoto (Free / Premium £30/year): Another motorcycle routing app with a strong community sharing routes. Good UK coverage and a nice riding mode interface designed for gloves.
  • Google Maps (Free): Still the best for finding services, checking opening hours, and general navigation. Download offline areas before rural riding.
  • What3Words (Free): Divides the entire world into 3m squares, each with a unique three-word address. Used by UK emergency services. If you crash in the middle of nowhere, this app tells rescuers exactly where you are.

Weather Apps

  • Met Office (Free): The most accurate UK weather forecasting. Hour-by-hour forecasts, excellent weather warnings, and a great rain radar.
  • Yr.no (Free): Norwegian weather service with surprisingly detailed UK forecasts. Particularly good for mountain and coastal areas.
  • Windy (Free): Visual weather radar showing rain, wind, and cloud movement in real-time. Brilliant for watching approaching weather systems and making routing decisions.

Fuel and Services

  • PetrolPrices (Free): Find the cheapest fuel near you. Shows station locations, opening hours, and current prices. Filters by fuel type.
  • Waze (Free): Community-reported traffic, hazards, and fuel prices. Better for urban areas than rural, but useful for avoiding congestion on touring approaches.

Accommodation

  • Booking.com (Free): Huge selection of B&Bs, hotels, and guesthouses with instant booking. Read reviews from motorcyclists. Filter by parking availability.
  • Pitchup.com (Free): UK campsite finder and booking platform. Shows availability, facilities, and prices. Filter by motorcycle-friendly features.
  • Park4Night (Free / Premium £4): Originally for campervans, but useful for finding overnight parking, wild camping spots, and unofficial stopping places.

Route Planning and Recording

  • Scenic (Free / Premium £10/year): Motorcycle-specific route recorder that tracks your ride, plots it on a map, and creates shareable ride logs with photos.
  • Relive (Free / Premium): Creates 3D flyover videos of your ride using GPS data. Great for sharing your tour on social media.
  • RideWithGPS (Free / Premium): Detailed route planner with elevation profiles. Good for planning mountain pass routes where gradient matters.
Before your tour, install and test every app. Download offline data for your touring area. Make sure notifications are set correctly — you don't want a social media ping distracting you at 60mph. And carry a power bank — all these apps will drain your battery.

Communication

  • WhatsApp: Group chats for touring groups. Share locations, photos, and updates at rest stops.
  • Cardo / Sena apps: If you use a Bluetooth intercom, the companion app handles pairing, settings, and firmware updates.

Before You Ride: Setup Checklist

  • Download all offline maps for your route area
  • Set apps to do-not-disturb mode while riding
  • Enable location sharing with your safety contact
  • Test your phone mount and charging setup
  • Back up your phone before departure

The right apps turn your phone from a distraction into an indispensable touring tool. Set up once, and they'll work for you every mile of every tour.
keyTakeaways: OS Maps (£24/year) is the standard for detailed UK offline mapping; Kurviger and Calimoto excel at scenic routing.
What3Words (free) pinpoints your exact location for emergency services, even offline.
For weather, combine the Met Office, Yr.no and Windy for wind and rain detail.
PetrolPrices finds cheap fuel and Park4Night and Pitchup help with camping and stopovers.
Download offline maps and set up every app before you leave signal behind.

faq.q: What is the best navigation app for UK motorcycle touring?
faq.a: It depends on your priority. OS Maps at £24 a year offers unrivalled detailed UK mapping with offline download, ideal for remote areas. Kurviger (free, or £20/year premium) and Calimoto (free, or £30/year premium) specialise in curvy, scenic routing that avoids dull motorways. Many riders use OS Maps for detail and Kurviger for planning the fun roads.

faq.q: Which apps help in an emergency?
faq.a: What3Words is essential and free: it divides the world into 3-metre squares each with a unique three-word address, so you can give emergency services your exact location even where there is no postcode or road name. The app works offline for referencing your location, though you still need signal to make the call.

faq.q: What weather apps should I use?
faq.a: Combine several for a fuller picture. The Met Office app gives reliable official UK forecasts, Yr.no is excellent for hour-by-hour precipitation, and Windy is superb for visualising wind strength and rain bands, which matters greatly on a bike. Check all three the evening before and again in the morning, as UK weather changes fast.

faq.q: Do touring apps work without phone signal?
faq.a: Only if you prepare. Apps like OS Maps, Kurviger and Calimoto let you download offline maps in advance, which is essential because much of the Highlands, mid-Wales and remote England has no coverage. Set up your routes, download the relevant map tiles, and test everything at home before you ride into signal-free country.
